newsitem.title: USA: US AIDE SAYS IRISH EMBARASSED BY NEW MAD COW CASE.
newsitem.headline: US AIDE SAYS IRISH EMBARASSED BY NEW MAD COW CASE.

text.p: A new case of mad cow disease discovered in Ireland is "somewhat of an embarrassment" to the Irish government, a U.S. Agriculture Department aide stationed in Dublin said.

In a August 8 report released Wednesday, the attache said the latest case of mad cow disease, or bovine spongiform encephalopathy, was found on a "state-run dairy research farm" in Moorepark, County Cork.
"Teagasc, the operator of the research facility, now faces the loss of its dairy research base as its 500 prime dairy animals face slaughter," the attache said.
Under Irish government rules, the whole herd must be "depopulated," the attache said.

"The Moorepark facility is well known internationally for dairy research and the loss of the herd, built up over many years, will be a severe setback both to ongoing and planned research," the attache said.
It is not known how the animal, aged between four and five years, was infected.

However, it is suspected that it may have been infected by feeds containing offal and spinal and bone tissue prior to the Irish government's ban on the feeding of such high-risk material to livestock, the attache said.
